title: Notes of Ministry - 16 - March 1974

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 16 - March 1974 (2054)/Notes of Ministry - 16 - March - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: We have often referred to the way the Lord secured the writer of these verses and what his history was, especially at its beginnings with God. The scripture tells us what took place, or much that took place, when Paul, the writer of these verses, was stricken down on his way to Damascus by an appearing of the Lord to him from heaven—wonderful beginning of the path with God of one that God signally used—Paul. It struck me, as I thought about him, that a very important thing is not just how he began, and not just how we began, but what our present link with Christ really is.

There might have been a falling away; I do not mean with the writer of these words, I need scarcely say; there might have been with me a falling away. Maybe today is not our best day thus far. I believe the Lord would speak to us about that, what He is to us today. What is our appreciation of Him today? Where are we in this precious pathway of committal to the interests of Christ today, and what is our outlook this very day? For these verses were written not at the beginning of his pathway in God’s testimony, but as we understand very close to the end. What a pathway it had been, as the history shows. Paul had his beginnings, remarkable beginnings. I expect everyone here, every mature person anyway, has had beginnings, and some of them have been remarkable beginnings, not always miraculous beginnings in an outward sense but remarkable enough in an inward sense when the Lord spoke to us; but where do we stand in reference to Him and His interests today?

This man, as he wrote these words, as we understand from what he writes, was in prison, but how feelingly he writes of God’s calling, and what the calling is; and he also writes about “the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ”. You cannot read these verses without sensing the depth of feeling with which the beloved writer speaks of the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, that which is the central point of the whole situation to which he is referring. What a glorious presentation we have here of what He has done, setting out in a few words the immensity of His work, “who has annulled death”. How briefly that is put, yet how immense the cost was in suffering! Whose sufferings? The sufferings of “our Saviour Jesus Christ”; He

“annulled death”, he says. What a wonderful thing it is at this present time, as we think of the incidence of death in this dark scene in which we are, to think of the brevity, the power, with which the writer of these verses could present a glorious Person who has annulled death, has met and set aside its power—not that its power does not remain in the sense of the article of it and the bearing it has on men.

He is calling attention to One who has annulled death. Think of a Person of whom that can be said. You know who the Person is. Thank God I know who this Person is. This very scripture makes that perfectly plain, but I ask you just to ponder for a moment the immensity of the power of death being annulled by one glorious Man. God would bring some sense of His power into our souls as we preach, or listen to the preaching—the might of delivering power in the hand of God through the efficacy of the work of Jesus. It is towards you to set you perfectly free, to give you and sustain with you a link with this glorious Person that shall go right through. Are you looking back, beloved friend, on brighter days? Does any one of us here look back on brighter times in our histories? The Lord would have to say to us this afternoon if that is so. He would have these times, these times remarkable in their place and way, to be our best times. Maybe for any one of us there shall be better yet, but has something come in to rob us of the real appreciation of Christ and of the glad tidings of which He is the precious Theme and Centre? Has anything come in like that?

See how this man writes at the end of his time, “I know whom I have believed”. How the enemy has sought to bring in many a diversion in the history of us all, many a taunt, many a lie to divert; but here is a man who says, “I know whom I have believed”. He has a secure assurance in his soul. It is the constant effort of the enemies of Christ, of the enemies of God, of the enemies of the assembly, to bring in some lying diversion from what is precious to Christ and fruitful to God. How many of us have experienced the bitter thrusts of a defeated foe, for such he is. Thank God we know the One by whom he has been defeated. Let us remember that; let us say, as this writer says, “I know whom I have believed”, and continue in the sense of strength, the sense of being stabilized in realising that our hope is in Christ; our hope in that sense is in God. Our resource, our immediate resource, is in the Spirit; our objective, Christ in glory, the same glorious Person of Jesus.

Has somebody, or something, sought to divert you from a clear view of Christ as He is? What is the present situation? There may have been brighter situations in past history. The Lord would say, Why is this so? What is it that has come in? Here is a man who went on from strength to strength and can write thus very close to the end of his days. It is not that he did not make mistakes, I am not suggesting that, but his end is the bright, radiant, happy enjoyment of a sustained link with Christ in his soul, something which he can fall back upon as the enemy makes fresh thrusts. A man in prison circumstances with nothing of an outward kind, I suppose, for his comfort or encouragement, far otherwise; but his hope is in God, his faith is in Christ, his resource is in the Spirit, his links are with the saints of the assembly, to one of whom he is writing so feelingly, this beloved child of his, Timothy.

There are some Timothys here, young men seeking to follow in the Pauline course, and I would address myself feelingly to such, to young men and young women, that there may indeed be a following of a Pauline course, nothing less. Let us seek, in our time, in grace and strength which God gives, to stand for nothing less than what Paul stood for. You may say, ‘I am not a Paul’. I am not suggesting that you are. Paul was an apostle; the Lord appointed him. But the path that he set on is the christian pathway in its true and essential character. He set on a path in which those who have followed in faithfulness to Christ have continued. You say, ‘What about those Dark Ages?’ God knows. It is not for you and me to reason about the Dark Ages, the point is today; where do I stand today? In what path are my steps today? And if I may make so bold as to ask the direct question, In what path are your steps today? Is it the Pauline way? There was a time, you know, in his journeys when Paul made a “straight course”. Thank God there is a straight course today. The enemy would love to introduce all kinds of diversions into that straight course, but there is a straight course to be taken in dependence upon the Lord, in reliance upon the Spirit.

So he speaks of God “who has saved us, and has called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace”. It is remarkable how he looks back over things and sees how it all has its origin in God and His grace, “according to his own purpose and grace”; that is, he sees that he was in God’s heart for blessing, and he sees how God came in in grace to effect his blessing. He goes right back to his beginnings in the sense that his beginnings were in the heart of God. He did not achieve his own blessing; he was set on a totally different course, persecuting the assembly, but divine grace wrought; “according to his own purpose and grace”. God came into this man’s history, engaged him with Christ, and brought him to submission to Christ; and that is the great point to which we so often have to come back.

If some diversion has come, if I am not as bright and happy and free with Christ and in the truth today as I was, maybe six months ago or at some prior time, let me ask myself, ‘Am I a truly submissive person to the One who is established of God, as another scripture reminds us, “Lord and Christ”?’ We spoke of that this afternoon, but I feel the vital point of real submission to the Lord. That is how this man began such a course as this. We may have begun that way, and something may have come in just to interrupt our submissive course in relation to Christ. What is the present situation? That the heart of God is toward us, “according to his own purpose and grace”; we were in His heart long, long before He ever was in ours in any sense at all. Grace took us up just as we were in our sins, in our need, we might say in our yielding to flesh; all these things marked us, but God came in in His own grace and turned us to Jesus, as Paul says here, “our Saviour Jesus Christ”.

What a Saviour! What sufferings He endured! What a laying down of His life we have to think of; that occupied us a little this morning. He laid down His life; in that sense it was not that men slew Him. It was their intention to slay Him and they did put Him on the cross to die, and it was their intention He should die; but He laid down His life; He did that. Men could not take the life of the Son of God; men could not take the life of Jesus; He laid it down. He laid it down for you, He laid it down for me, He laid it down for myriads of the redeemed. What a Saviour! This is all in the grace of which the writer speaks; it is all to meet your case, not only at its beginnings but in its continuance.

It has in mind the way in which every one of us shall continue to find Christ in every fresh eventuality of the pathway, and to find in Him, “our Saviour Jesus Christ”. That is the whole bearing of what is in that Person toward us in the course of these present things. He is “our Saviour Jesus Christ”, there is always saving power there whatever may beset us, whatever fresh temptation may come, whatever fresh diversion may be attempted; He is our Saviour, and the saving power is ever to be known and proved by us, “our Saviour Jesus Christ”.

Paul says the calling “has been made manifest now by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who has annulled death, and brought to light life and incorruptibility by the glad tidings”; “life and incorruptibility”. Life in Him? Yes, but far more, life for you; there is incorruptibility in Himself as He is, certainly, but it stands related to what is incorruptible in you, in me, in men. I am not speaking of actual incorruptibility yet whilst we are yet in these bodies, but I am calling attention to the blessed fact that God has incorruptibility in view, an incorruptible order of things, an order of things into which sin and decline can never come. And He would sustain you by the Spirit in the gain of what is established incorruptibly in the Person of His beloved Son. How much there is in this dark scene to corrupt; but God would say, ‘I will give you a link in faith and in the gift of the Spirit with that which is incorruptible’ as He turns you to that glorious, risen, ascended, exalted Man where He is. He has “brought to light life and incorruptibility by the glad tidings”.

Do you value the glad tidings? Are they glad tidings to you? Is there something holding someone from what I might speak of as the gladness of the glad tidings, the spring of joy of appreciation of Christ, the enjoyment of the gift of the Spirit, a place in relation to His interests here? Oh what joy is in these things! I would say again to you, (just to turn you if I may to the Lord about it) Was there a time when the joy was greater? Was there a time when the joy was brighter? Why is it?

Here the beloved apostle, after a long course of devoted service, of eventful history spiritually and circumstantially, says, “I know whom I have believed”. Oh, I love the definiteness, the, sense of assurance which he conveys! How stable is a man who has gone on in his history, has found His links with Christ to be his true strength, and has found the known gift of the Spirit to be his constant ever-faithful present resource. You may find all this; you may find it not just momentarily, certainly not just passingly, but find it as the characteristic spring of your life, a link with a glorified Christ and realisation of power here known to you in the gift of the Spirit. Why should these things not be yours? God is toward you in them; the glad tidings go out. In some sense this scripture brings its own voice in true glad tidings irrespective of what a preacher may say. Here is this precious scripture coming home to you. Why should you not come into the gain of the same resource that Paul knew, to know the same Saviour that Paul knew, to drink into the same Spirit that Paul drank into, to find yourself in principle and in life in the same company that Paul found his life in?

These things are to be yours, though he says, “For which cause also I suffer these things”. The present moment, he would say, is a moment of suffering. We do not know in detail what those sufferings were. His being in prison would be among them, but I doubt if that would be his only element of suffering. He was suffering in the sense of departures from Christ and from the truth, but he says, “I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed”. Well, is this our brightest moment? The Lord would speak to us this evening just to revive us, maybe; such is His grace, He loves to revive. He would search out things, if something has come in between Himself and any one of us, that we might be able to be alongside of Paul in what his present link with Christ is, as he says, “I know whom I have believed”. May we thus be under God’s good hand and continue under His hand, for His name’s sake.

The reference to the Father’s house and to the matter of watching came into our earlier conversation and I feel, beloved brethren, that both have a very significant importance. The actuality of the Father’s house is a future thought; it is a sphere of things where the Father Himself finds His pleasure and where things are arranged and ordered in such a way that the Person whose house it is is ministered to for His own satisfaction.

I believe we are able to touch the affections that belong to it, and the liberty that is proper there, in spirit, in the power of the Holy Spirit, even now, and that in the sense of being there in association with the Lord Jesus. But we are looking forward to the time when what we now touch in spirit will be an abiding and uninterrupted experience that will minister eternally to the Father’s pleasure; when the responsive affections that belong to sonship, so perfectly reciprocated in the full sense of what that word means by the Lord Jesus as Man here upon earth, will be, by way of extension, the Father’s portion in the response of His sons.

The coming of the Lord has a vital and distinct bearing upon this side of the truth. Ofttimes we may be inclined to think just of the relief that will be ours, the setting free from the incubus of what we are according to nature, and the test that the flesh is, as distinct from nature—sinful flesh that would raise its head at any time. We are inclined to think of the relief of being actually and practically set free from these things to have a full and uninhibited part in response to the Father’s heart. That is very blessed, very real, something to be looked forward to surely—but not the greatest thing.
One would not underestimate the greatness of any one result of the sufferings of Jesus. Think of what it will be to be clear of every hindrance. Would you not like to be like that? I would!

But evil thoughts can even now be dismissed in the Spirit’s power immediately; let us not concede that evil thoughts cannot be dismissed, because they can, but then evil thoughts will never get an entrance because of the character of the Person who is there. But that is not the greatest thing.

I believe the greatest thing is that the Father will have in His house those who will minister to His own pleasure. Think of the satisfaction of a Father’s heart in the felicitous relationship of His sons, where love is free and where love is expressed and where there is an environment that is conducive to all that love rejoices in. This is the Father’s house. I believe that the Spirit would help us to get away from what is geographical and would help us in relation to what is moral and what is spiritual. I think we always need that, to get away from the idea of what is geographical. What is moral and what is spiritual is just as real, in fact more real, and the Holy Spirit is on our side to help us to touch these things.

Now the Lord speaks to His own at a time of crisis—a time of tremendous crisis. A betrayer had already been brought to light and had departed from the circle where Jesus was loved. He went immediately out and it was night. How the Lord Jesus felt that One who would deny Him was yet to come to light. How He felt that too. And He Himself was about to depart to the Father and His own were to be left in the place of testimony. This is the situation, and He says, “Let not your heart be troubled; ye believe on God, believe also on me”. Beloved, I think the Spirit would help us to hold the Person of our Lord Jesus Christ in a constant way in our minds and in our affections, and when I say ‘in our affections’ I mean to hold Him as loving Him all the time. That is what I mean; I do not use it in any technical sense at all, but as loving Him all the time.

“Believe also on me. In my Father’s house there are many abodes; were it not so, I had told you”; think of the confidence, think of the intimacy, think of the regard that He had for His own. Is it any less today? Does anybody think that it is any less today? The constancy of His love is something to be relied upon, something to be trusted in, something to quell every thought of unbelief, because it is a question of believing on Him. This would silence any infidel thoughts. And He adds, “Were it not so, I had told you: for I go to prepare you a place”. The object of His going He states categorically, “I go to prepare you a place”. As believing on Him we believe that too.

It is a prepared place, it means that care and activity, the activity of holy love, are in it. How He must regard the persons for whom the place is prepared! Would that we had a deeper appreciation of what the greatness of the love of Christ is—not only for each one of us personally, but His love for His own as together. It is not exactly the assembly in John, but

the personnel of the assembly, the persons who compose it. And so He says, “I go to prepare you a place; and if I go and shall prepare you a place, I am coming again and shall receive you”. To the place? Oh no, “To myself”. Is not that precious? Of course the place is what it is because of the One who is there—“To myself, that where I am ye also may be.”

Now when He said it, what He said as to His going was future, but in our day it is an accomplished fact. He has actually gone, but He said, “I am coming again and shall receive you to myself”. We might say, is not this to be known in the Spirit even now? I think the power of it is to be known, but the actuality of it is future. It is a glorious prospect that every believer in Jesus is entitled to have. Whether every believer in Jesus really lays hold of it is something else, but the title to it is theirs on account of Himself and what He has done. He says, I “shall receive you to myself”. For whose satisfaction is that? His!

I believe the Spirit, dear brethren, would, help us to adjust our thinking, that we might begin to think from Himself. I think that is worth dwelling on; to begin to think from Himself in everything—for it makes a wonderful difference: It makes a difference practically, it makes a difference in the testimony practically, and it makes a difference spiritually too, to begin to think from Himself. You know, if we begin to think from the right point our thoughts are right, but if we are slightly off the right point our thoughts are inclined to be off the point too.

And so He says, “I … shall receive you to myself, that where I am ye also may be”. Now we know where Jesus is; we know that even now, for through Him and by the Spirit we have access to the Father. We know that; but we are to be there in that holy environment of perfect love into which nothing that is unsuited has ever intruded. These things, beloved, we lay hold of, not only in faith, but by the Spirit’s power. And they are to affect us. I would raise that with you as I raise it with myself.

Are we really affected by these things? Do we really believe them? I do not mean mere acquiescence of mind, I mean in the activity of faith. And the activity of faith means that I am governed by what I believe. Now the present moment is a waiting time, because He says, “I am coming again and shall receive you to myself, that where I am ye also may be”. You may say, ‘How long is it?’ We were saying in the reading it may be today. Who could define the waiting time? There is only one Person who knows when the time is, and that is the Father Himself.
Meanwhile, whilst we would be on the tiptoe of expectation, we are not to be inactive.

Certain things are committed into the hands of the Son. The Father loves the Son and has given all things to be in His hand. That is not just one thing—it is everything. So it says in Mark 13, “It is as a man gone out of the country”, (but he is coming back) having left his house and given to his bondmen the authority, and to each one his work, and commanded the door-keeper that he should watch”. What holy activity is to be entered into! Whose activity is it, whose interests?—His! The question was raised with Jesus, “By what authority doest thou these things?” (Matthew 21: 23). He raised certain questions that His opposers failed to answer and therefore He did not tell them by what authority He did them, but He tells us. It is the authority, it is His authority; the Lord’s authority. Who is He? The One who is absolutely supreme. He gave to His bondmen the authority. To do what? To do His work, the authority to do His work.
And then it says, “And commanded the door-keeper that he should watch”. What is the doorkeeper watching for? I think he is watching for the master. And while he is watching (and

he is watching all the time) do you think he will let into the master’s house anything that is unsuited to that master? I think, beloved, that the maintenance of what is suited to the Lord is guaranteed as we are watching for Him personally. I feel persuaded that that is right. All the time the doorkeeper was watching he had been watching for his lord. As the Lord says, “Watch therefore, for ye do not know when the master of the house comes—evening, or midnight, or cock-crow, or morning; lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping”.

Watching for Him will guarantee that nothing that is unsuited to Him will be allowed to enter into the house. Is that how you regard the local assembly? As watching for Him, nothing that is unsuited to Him will be allowed to enter that house. You say, ‘Who is the door-keeper?’ I am; you are’. ‘Oh’, but you say, ‘there is other work’. Yes, but door-keeping belongs to everybody, it belongs to the boys and the girls at school. You are a door-keeper. It belongs to these young folk just starting out in life, in their businesses; you are a door-keeper, you are watching for Him. It belongs to the more mature persons: it belongs to the housewives at home; pre-eminently it belongs to those who have regard for what is due to Him in the local assembly, that is where it is exercised.

And so He says in the verse that we read, “Take heed, watch and pray”. That is watching in dependence. It is not watching in self-confidence, it is watching in dependence “Watch and pray”. And then He says in the last verse, “But what I say to you, I say to all, Watch”. Let us watch ourselves in regard to what is unsuited, but primarily watch for Him. If that could be conveyed here and now it would be well worth while our being here. Let us watch for Him.

In Acts 20 there is the matter of the local assembly and the responsible element in it is addressed. Paul called the elders over from Ephesus and laid this charge upon them, and having laid the charge upon them he says that he is clean from the blood of all, “For I have not shrunk from announcing to you all the counsel of God”. But he says, “Take heed therefore to yourselves, and to all the flock, wherein the Holy Spirit has set you as overseers, to shepherd the assembly of God”. When the Lord refers to the flock in John he says, in regard of it, “one flock”. That is a feature of the flock, “one flock; one shepherd”.

Here Paul refers to the flock, “all the flock, wherein the Holy Spirit has set you as overseers” (that is, the local expression of it) “to shepherd the assembly of God”. That is, the saints are regarded in the light of what the assembly is universally. You say, ‘Why do you say that?’

Because, dear brethren, we are responsible in our own locality, but we are linked with the saints universally who walk in this light. The idea of independency in the local assembly is foreign to what is proper to the assembly. I believe that needs to be underlined at the present

time. I believe we need to re-affirm before the Lord our allegiance to the truth as to the assembly in its universal bearing. The fact is that the expression of it as we walk in that light is to be substantially seen in the localities where we are. And of what value it is! “The assembly of God, which he has purchased with the blood of his own”.

The idea of purchase is that what is purchased becomes the possession of the One who so valued it that He was prepared to pay the price needed to have it for Himself. So the apostle brings us in, not only for us to understand how God values the assembly, but that we might value it in the same way. So Paul speaks about what will enter in. Nothing will enter in, of course, up there. It is down here where things enter in, these perverted things, things that are off-centre—that do not begin with Christ. That is perversion. They are viewed from some other consideration. Do you know something about that? I do—consideration for persons rather than for Him. It is very near, it is nearer perhaps than some of us would like to concede.

These responsible people were to watch. Paul says, “Wherefore watch”. And he brings himself forward, in his comely way, as if to say, ‘I have watched night and day. Not only have I watched night and day but I have served night and day; served in watching’. And what is he watching for? That what is so valuable to God, and for which He has been prepared to pay such a price, might be preserved for His pleasure until it is translated, taken to a place where watching will never be needed any more.

Meanwhile, beloved, to your heart and mine, on account of what is precious to Christ, in such a scene as this is, the word is, Watch. It is His own word. It is the Spirit’s word through the apostle, but what I am seeking to convey, if I can, is the necessity for watching on account of what is so precious to God and to Christ. May we be helped and value more and more what He has, and be alerted, stimulated and revitalised in regard to the imminent return of the One who will come again to receive us to Himself. May God bless the word.

It is noticeable that this prophet Zechariah is quoted more in Matthew’s gospel than in the other gospels, which would no doubt have a bearing on what was said earlier, that in a time of recovery we are to be brought back to the original truth as to the assembly. The truth was opened up by Paul. As he says, it was given to him “to complete the word of God”,

Colossians 1: 25. But it is wonderful that we can get right back to the words of the Lord Jesus and what He would say about “my assembly”. So I thought we should occupy ourselves with the Lord Jesus Himself, because in Him there is always food for our souls and there our affections are always stimulated.

The connection I see between these two scriptures is that they both refer to the sufferings of the Lord Jesus in the house of His friends. Psalm 55 refers to “my familiar friend” (Psalm 55: 13), and Zechariah refers to “the house of my friends” (Zechariah 13: 6). I believe we should therefore have feelings, beloved, in relation to what has come in in the way of departure in the recovery and the way in which we have ourselves failed and have added, may we say, to these sufferings. They would be like the sufferings of which it speaks in John’s gospel, “He came to his own, and his own received him not”, John 1: 11. But then, over against, all that, it says that “as many as received him, to them gave he the right to be children of God”. So that as our hearts are affected by the sufferings of Jesus, and as all the sorrows that have come in among us turn us afresh to those sufferings, we can experience the blessing afresh, and what it is to be brought into relationship with God. Features which these scriptures show in contrast are, on the one hand, the wonderful place that the Lord Jesus took in humanity, and, on the other, the greatness of His place as Jehovah’s Fellow. It says in the epistle to the Philippians, “taking his place in the likeness of men”, Philippians 2: 7. None other could take the place that Jesus took, and yet how real His humanity was; indeed, apart from the reality of the manhood of Jesus there would be no blessing for us.

This verse has always been a source of wonder to me, “It was thou, a man mine equal, my intimate, my familiar friend”. The note tells us that the word for ‘man’ is ‘Enosh’, that is, weak, mortal man. To think that Jesus would speak of His familiar friend this way, that He would say, “a man”, that is weak, mortal man, “mine equal”. Not that Jesus was weak, mortal man, far be the thought—as it says in another psalm, “I have laid help upon a mighty one”, Psalm 89; 19. Think of the power and the might of Jesus; think of who He was in the glory of His Person, as it says in the scripture in Zechariah, “against the man”, that is, the mighty Man, “that is my fellow”. How wonderful that He should take in lowly grace such a place as to say, ‘a weak mortal man Mine equal’, and yet such is the glory of His Person that Jehovah Himself could speak of Him as “the man that is my fellow”.

So we see the feelings of the Lord Jesus expressed in this psalm, and it would help us to know His feelings at the present time as despised and rejected of men, Isaiah 53: 3. We have just witnessed in the open-air preaching that there is no room for the Lord Jesus in the world at the present time. And yet here in speaking of one with whom He had sweet intercourse He was saying that He could have borne it if it had been an enemy, but it was “thou, a man mine equal, mine intimate, my familiar friend”. So how the Lord Jesus would feel all that has come in among us, and how our hearts would be drawn to Him as we ourselves come to a judgment of all that has transpired, not in a general way, but as each one searches his own heart. It is very wonderful that in all this there should be a positive result with us. We can see that the hand of the Lord Jesus has been over everything. The Father has committed everything into the hands of the Son; things have never got out of hand, so that everything is designed towards this great end that we should have a greater appreciation of the love of the Lord Jesus, a greater understanding of His Person and of His manhood, and a greater knowledge of God.

So we can review what is past with this positive end in view and find food for our souls and be refreshed in relation to our affections as we take account not of what we have suffered, but of the feelings of Jesus. How much we owe to the expressions of the psalmist and of the prophets. The Spirit of Christ in them gives expression to words which show to us certain feelings of Jesus, in the perfection of His humanity, which are not recorded in the gospel narratives. As we go over them together we can understand these feelings, and as we may have been called to suffer in some little measure we can enter into them. They would draw out our hearts to our blessed Lord in relation to all that He has suffered.

We have in Zechariah the way in which everything has been met. There is, on the one hand, what He suffered in the house of His friends, there are the wounds in His hands. Those were the hands into which everything had been committed and in which He was carrying everything through for the glory of God; but the time came when God’s judgment sword was awakened against His Shepherd, against, as it says, “the man that is my fellow”. He alone could bear the judgment, involving as it did that He should bear the penalty and go into death itself so that there might be a way out for us. But now He is presented to us in glory as an Object for faith, and we can go to the mountain and we can find wood. We can look to Jesus the Leader and Completer of faith (Hebrews 12: 2) if we are tested, and if we suffer we see Jesus the One who suffered as no other, and we can see Him there as our great High Priest, the One who is able to save completely all who come to God by Him, Hebrews 7: 25. What a wonderful result of the pressure and the suffering that may have been our portion, if we have a clearer view of Jesus, the Leader and Completer of faith.

Then it speaks here of the two times of testing, and I would suggest that this is like what we have passed through in recent years. “It shall come to pass in all the land, saith Jehovah, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein”. It is not the majority. See what happened in 1970—if we had gone with the majority, where would we be today?

But it says, “the third shall be left”. But then again that was not sufficient in the way in which the Lord was operating to secure His own end, and so it says, “I will bring the third part into the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried”. But what an end, beloved—“They shall call on my name, and I will answer them; I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, Jehovah is my God”. Think of these wonderful relationships that we were speaking of on Lord’s day—and not only speaking of them but enjoying the reality of them—what it is to have that message coming freshly to us, “My Father and your Father … my God and your God”, John 20: 17. They are wonderful experiences that we have as we enter into the greatness of God’s thoughts for men, and as we enjoy them He enters into “the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints”, Ephesians 1: 18.

So let us be encouraged; let us see what the end is in these things. It may have been necessary, after the testing, to bring again through the fire, but it would be in view of vessels being secured in view of the service of God. Everything is secured on the basis of the sufferings of the Lord Jesus, so that we would not be occupied with what we have passed through and what we have suffered, but with the One who has secured everything for God.
May the Lord bless the word.

“THIS WOMAN, WHO IS A DAUGHTER OF ABRAHAM”—The woman in Luke 13 did not look like a daughter of Abraham. For eighteen years she had been “bent together and wholly unable to lift her head up”. But the Lord held for her the dignity which belonged to her. How cheering! If Satan has bound any of us, perhaps for a long time, and we look back wistfully to days of freedom and joy, the Lord holds for us our early committals and the dignity which, in one sense, we have relinquished. In Him is full resource to restore us. This woman was “made straight, and glorified God”. She was manifestly now a daughter of Abraham, to whom Jehovah said, “Walk before my face, and be perfect”, Genesis 17: l.

“THE FURY OF MAN SHALL PRAISE THEE”—(Psalm 76: 10)—How often has this occurred! Paul is imprisoned in Rome—thence flows out his richest, choicest ministry. John is banished to the isle of Patmos—he receives the wondrous Revelation of the ways of God. To take a much later, less exalted example, John Bunyan is thrown into Bedford jail for 12 years—and we get the “Pilgrim’s Progress”.

“FAITH’S EYES ARE ON THE GOAL”—No doubt this line of the hymn is based on Philippians 3: 14. There is a great need for this to mark us. Troubles arise, and it is easy to be absorbed with them. Let us keep our eyes on the goal. The divine end is that we are to be “conformed to the image of his Son”, (Romans 8: 29), while the assembly will come down “out of the heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned, for her husband”, (Revelation 21: 2). Present pressures in the testimony, and in our circumstances, are divinely intended for our education and formation—not to divert us from the goal, but to form us for it. As going through the difficulties with God we can look beyond them and get a clearer view of the assured end to which, in all His ways with His people, God is working.
